headline: Red Sox bats go cold and Patriots drop painful Seattle opener
morning_brew: That four to six loss to the Angels at Fenway was a flat-out disaster, and watching the bats sleepwalk for eight innings took about three years off my life. Jake Bennett had a hell of a time finding the zone early, and while the bullpen finally decided to show up and stabilize the middle frames, the hole we dug was way too deep to climb out of. It is the kind of game that makes you wanna throw your Dunks at the wall, especially with the wild card spot on the line. Stringing together hits when the pressure is actually building shouldn't be this hard, but somehow we made it look like rocket science.

The football season kicked off with a kick to the gut as the Patriots stumbled ten to thirteen in a defensive slog against Seattle. Drake Maye looked like he was playing against ghosts out there, and walking away from the opener with a loss is a brutal way to start the year. Then you hear A.J. Brown is dealing with a sprained ankle and the misery just piles up. We need some major adjustments on offense before this thing gets out of hand, because searching for answers in week one is exactly the kind of frustration I thought we left in the past.

We have a rare night off from the diamond, and honestly, it is probably for the best so we can all stop pacing around the living room. The team needs to clear its head before the Royals come to town, and I am praying a little time away from the Fens helps the lineup find its pulse again. My neighbor Rick is already four hours into an investigation regarding why we didn't trade for a bat in July, and while he is losing his mind, I am just gonna enjoy a quiet night and hope the luck changes when the action returns.

news_digest.headline: Source: Patriots' A.J. Brown likely out at least 4 weeks
news_digest.dans_take: Four weeks without our top target is a nightmare scenario for this offense.
